Definition Enriched_of_TwoPreorder (P : TwoPreorder) : @Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal := @Build_Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal (tpre_carrier P) (ehom_of_le P) _ _ _ _ _  (eid built from tpre_refl, ecompose from tpre_trans, and the three coherence obligations closed by `apply two_thin`) — the class instantiated at a base that IS a monoidal preorder (V = Bool), which is the shape Def 2.46 assumes

statement_record.book: Given a symmetric monoidal preorder V = (V, ≤, I, ⊗), a V-category X consists of a set Ob(X) and, for each ordered pair x, y of objects, a hom-OBJECT X(x,y) ∈ V, subject to exactly two inequalities and no equational data: (a) I ≤ X(x,x) for every x, and (b) X(x,y) ⊗ X(y,z) ≤ X(x,z) for all x, y, z. The book remarks that symmetry of V is not needed for the definition itself (only conditions (a)-(c) of Def 2.2), though it is needed later for products of V-categories.
statement_record.intree: Class Enriched (K : Category) `{@Monoidal K} := { eobj : Type; ehom : eobj → eobj → K; eid {x} : I ~{K}~> (x ⟿ x); ecompose {x y z} : (y ⟿ z) ⨂ (x ⟿ y) ~{K}~> (x ⟿ z); eid_left; eid_right; ecompose_assoc }
statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance, intree-stronger in base generality. `ehom : eobj → eobj → K` is exactly clauses (i)-(ii) (the V-valued square matrix of hom-objects); `eid : I ~{K}~> (x ⟿ x)` is exactly axiom (a) I ≤ X(x,x) and `ecompose : (y ⟿ z) ⨂ (x ⟿ y) ~{K}~> (x ⟿ z)` exactly axiom (b) (the two tensor factors written in the opposite order — presentation only). The in-tree base is an arbitrary monoidal category and only `Monoidal` is required, NOT `SymmetricMonoidal`, matching the book's own remark that symmetry is not needed. Over a general (proof-relevant) base the class additionally DEMANDS the three Kelly coherence equations eid_left/eid_right/ecompose_assoc that Def 2.46 never states; over a preorder base these are vacuous and are discharged in-tree by thinness (Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:26 `two_thin : ∀ (f g : TwoHom x y), f = g`), so no extra hypothesis is imposed in the book's setting. Caveat (does not affect this item's claim but bites at Def 2.53): the library has no `MonoidalPreorder` class and no generic bridge turning a symmetric monoidal preorder into a thin monoidal category — a base must be hand-built, and exactly one such base exists in-tree, Two_Monoidal (Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:105, tensor := meet, unit := top). The book's parenthetical about products of V-categories has no in-tree counterpart (no product of enriched categories anywhere under Construction/Enriched/).

Lemma ehom_of_le_complete {P : TwoPreorder} {x y : tpre_carrier P} : tpre_le P x y → ehom_of_le P x y = TwoY  (with the companion `ehom_of_le_empty` at Two.v:122: (tpre_le P x y → False) → ehom_of_le P x y = TwoX) — the (x,y) entry of the truth-value matrix is `true` exactly when x ≤ y and `false` otherwise, the example's X(s,t) = true / X(t,s) = false computation

statement_record.book: Worked instance of Def 2.46 at V = Bool: from the preorder generated by a Hasse diagram on {p,q,r,s,t}, build a Bool-category X with Ob(X) the five elements and X(x,y) := true if x ≤ y, false otherwise (so X(s,t) = true, X(t,s) = false); axiom (a) true ≤ X(x,x) is reflexivity and axiom (b) X(x,y) ∧ X(y,z) ≤ X(x,z) is transitivity, so both hold. Announces the correspondence runs both ways. Continues with the general convention of displaying a V-category as a square matrix indexed by objects whose (x,y) entry is X(x,y), here a 5×5 true/false matrix.
statement_record.intree: Enriched_of_TwoPreorder (P : TwoPreorder) : @Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal with ehom_of_le P x y = TwoY iff x ≤ y (ehom_of_le_complete / ehom_of_le_empty), eid from tpre_refl, ecompose from tpre_trans; conversely TwoPreorder_of_Enriched reads reflexivity off eid and transitivity off ecompose.

statement_record.book: There is a one-to-one correspondence between preorders and Bool-categories. Forward: a preorder (P,≤) gives a Bool-category with Ob = P and X(x,y) := true iff x ≤ y. Backward: a Bool-category X gives a preorder on Ob(X) by x ≤ y iff X(x,y) = true; the axiom I ≤ X(x,x) forces X(x,x) = true (reflexivity) and X(x,y) ∧ X(y,z) ≤ X(x,z) forces transitivity. The text proves the backward direction and defers mutual-inverseness to Exercise 2.50.
statement_record.intree: Theorem Enriched_Two_preorder : @Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal ↔ TwoPreorder, with fst = TwoPreorder_of_Enriched (reflexivity from eid via two_from_top, transitivity from ecompose) and snd = Enriched_of_TwoPreorder.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the theorem's own claim, intree-stronger on the morphism level. Both CONSTRUCTIONS are in tree and their derivations are the book's: TwoPreorder_of_Enriched reads reflexivity off eid via two_from_top (Two.v:38, TwoHom TwoY z -> z = TwoY) and transitivity off ecompose under the meet, and the base is genuinely Bool (Two_Monoidal, Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:105, tensor := two_meet = AND, unit := TwoY = true). What is NOT in tree is the theorem's actual assertion. (1) `<->` is iffT (Lib/Foundation.v:72), a bare pair of functions with no inverse laws, so 'one-to-one correspondence' is not stated — iffT is satisfied by translations that lose information, and the bijection is precisely the content the book defers to Ex 2.50, also PARTIAL. (2) The right-hand side is not 'preorders' but DECIDABLE preorders: `TwoPreorder` (Two.v:60) carries `tpre_dec x y : tpre_le x y + (tpre_le x y -> False)` (Two.v:65) as a field, a hypothesis the classical statement does not carry, so the in-tree correspondence ranges over strictly fewer objects. This second restriction is constructively unavoidable for the literal base V = Bool (producing an element of the two-element TwoObj from a Type-valued relation IS a decision) and is disclosed in the file header, so it is a faithful constructive rendering rather than the reason for the PARTIAL. intree-stronger: EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone (Two.v:183) adds a morphism leg the book does not state here, `EnrichedFunctor _2 (snd Enriched_Two_preorder P) (snd Enriched_Two_preorder Q) <-> MonotoneMap P Q`.

gap: The 'one-to-one' half of the statement is missing. `Enriched_Two_preorder` (Construction/Enriched/Two.v:165) is `@Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal <-> TwoPreorder` with `<->` = iffT (Lib/Foundation.v:72), so it asserts only that each side can be translated into the other; nothing anywhere states that TwoPreorder_of_Enriched and Enriched_of_TwoPreorder are mutually inverse (no lemma in tree names both symbols), and therefore the theorem's claim that preorders and Bool-categories ARE the same thing is not formalized. This is the same missing content as 7sketches:2.3.2:ex50 and should be covered by one issue, not two: what is wanted is (a) tpre_le (TwoPreorder_of_Enriched (Enriched_of_TwoPreorder P)) x y <-> tpre_le P x y together with agreement of the decision procedure, and (b) ehom_of_le (TwoPreorder_of_Enriched E) x y = @ehom _ _ E x y, after which the correspondence can be packaged as a bijection/isomorphism rather than an iffT. The record's own facts support PARTIAL; only the boundary call differs, and the record's ex50 sibling already concedes the missing content ('never packaged as a bijection/isomorphism/equivalence'). Book Thm 2.49 STATES a one-to-one correspondence. In tree, Enriched_Two_preorder (Two.v:165, verified verbatim) is `@Enriched _2 Two_Monoidal <-> TwoPreorder` where `<->` is iffT (Lib/Foundation.v:72, confirmed: `Notation "x <-> y" := (iffT x y)`), i.e. a bare pair of functions carrying NO inverse laws — iffT permits translations that lose information, so 'one-to-one' is simply not asserted. That is a same-name-weaker-statement, the pattern this pass exists to catch, and classifying it PRESENT would tell a ledger reader there is nothing to do for the correspondence theorem itself. Second, independent shortfall found in my blind pass: the in-tree right-hand side is not 'preorders' but DECIDABLE preorders — `TwoPreorder` (Two.v:60) carries tpre_dec (Two.v:65) as a field — so the in-tree correspondence covers strictly fewer objects than the book's. I accept the record's defence that for the literal base V = Bool the decider is constructively unavoidable (one must compute an element of TwoObj), so this leg alone would not have overturned; the overturn rests on the bijectivity leg. Phase E should cover this item together with ex50 — the bijectivity gap is one piece of work, not two. evidence.intree_statement: Class Enriched (K : Category) `{@Monoidal K} := { eobj : Type; ehom : eobj → eobj → K; eid {x} : I ~{K}~> (x ⟿ x); ecompose {x y z} : (y ⟿ z) ⨂ (x ⟿ y) ~{K}~> (x ⟿ z); ... }  — the generic V-category class of which a Lawvere metric space is by definition the instance at V = Cost: `ehom` would be d, `eid` the law 0 ≥ d(x,x), `ecompose` the triangle inequality d(x,y) + d(y,z) ≥ d(x,z)

statement_record.book: A Lawvere metric space is by definition a Cost-category, where Cost = ([0,∞], ≥, 0, +) is the symmetric monoidal preorder of costs with the order REVERSED. Unpacked through Def 2.46: a set X = Ob(X) with d(x,y) := X(x,y) ∈ [0,∞] such that (a) 0 ≥ d(x,x), i.e. d(x,x) = 0, and (b) d(x,y) + d(y,z) ≥ d(x,z), the triangle inequality. Symmetry and separation are dropped and infinite distances allowed.
